StatementStandard__Description: Standard Sections: the parts of a statement that are the same on every job apart from the project they name (the TrueVision 3D Project Hub), the headings they are drawn from (the Contents) or the few fields they carry (the Document Header). Each one is switched on and off from the Statement Writer's edit bar (Standard Sections), lives in the statement's markdown as ONE marker line, and is drawn fresh from this file every time the statement is shown, printed or published - so a better sentence written here reaches every statement that carries the section, and the project's own name, code, link and QR code are always the ones on screen. The marker is a block like any picture: it can be dragged anywhere in the statement. Every value here is mirrored as a built-in default in the section's own module, so a failed fetch still draws the section.
StatementStandard__Order__Note: Adam, 29-Sep-2026, the order every statement opens in: 1. the header, 2. the header information, 3. the table of contents, 4. the TrueVision section, 5. the introduction. Each section's PlaceAfter keeps to it: the header takes over the top of the file, the Contents goes after the header's divider, the hub after the Contents. Every section but the header sits between two major dividers. It closes the same way every time: the Conclusion, the Drawing Schedule (above the footer), then the Document Footer, always last, under a divider of its own and none after it.

StatementStandard__DocumentHeader__Confi.DocumentHeader__Description: The statement's opening block: the company logo, the title and the header fields (Applicant, Site Address, Local Planning Authority, Prepared By, Document Version, and any others written). The fields are the job's own words and live INSIDE the marker, one a line - 'Label: value', with indented lines carrying a value on to more lines; 'Title' is the title and 'Logo' may replace the logo's address. Drawn with spacing of its own, so the document's heading rules (the minus two millimetres under every #####) cannot squeeze it - Adam, 29-Sep-2026: 'too constrained'. Switched on, it takes over a house header already at the top of the file; switched off, it writes that header back as markdown.
StatementStandard__DocumentHeader__Confi.DocumentHeader__LabelsWithoutColonNote: Labels drawn without a colon after them, as the house header always set 'Document Version' (bold, no colon) under 'Applicant:' and the rest.
DocumentHeader__NewFields: Local Planning Authority: [TO CONFIRM: local planning authority]
Prepared By: Mr Adam Noble of Noble Architecture
Document Version: Revision A  -  [TO CONFIRM: date]
StatementStandard__DocumentHeader__Confi.DocumentHeader__NewFieldsNote: What a statement with no header of its own is given when the section is switched on. Edit the card's marker to fill it in.

StatementStandard__Contents__Config.Contents__Description: The table of contents, drawn from the statement's own headings every time it is shown: each '### N.0 |' section, its '#### N.N |' subsections, any '##' part after the first section, and any other standard section that names a line for itself (the TrueVision 3D Project Hub). Two columns that never split a section; no page numbers, because a statement is one continuous page. It replaces the static list build_contents.py wrote, which fell behind the headings within the hour on RB05.
StatementStandard__Contents__Config.Contents__PlaceAfterNote: Straight after the divider that closes the header, with a divider of its own under it.
StatementStandard__Contents__Config.Contents__FallbackText: Standard Section: Table Of Contents. It is drawn from this statement's own headings by TrueVision's Statement Writer; this line is all an editor without it can show.

StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__Description: The TrueVision 3D Project Hub: a boxed section that sends the reader into the project's live 3D model with a QR code, a button and the short address, and tells them everything else the hub holds - every drawing, the specification, the document register and the statements. Built from the EB03 statement's section 18.0 (Interactive Online Tools) and Adam's brief of 29-Sep-2026: 'the ultimate nudge'. TOKENS in any text: {ProjectName} (the project's display name, or its code when it has none), {ProjectCode}, {ShortUrlText} (the short address without https://www.). Words written in the house comma-light rhythm for the paragraphs; the tiles and the access panel are captions and use ordinary punctuation.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__LabelNote: What the Standard Sections menu calls it.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__PlaceAfterNote: Where the section lands when it is switched on, tried in order: straight after the Contents (Standard:Contents - after the divider that closes it), else straight after the header's divider (HeaderDivider - the last major divider above the first numbered section). Adam, 29-Sep-2026, for every statement: 1. the header, 2. the header information, 3. the table of contents, 4. this section, 5. the introduction. It always sits between two major dividers, as its own section. Drag it to another section boundary afterwards.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__QrSizeMmNote: The symbol edge to edge on the A4 page, quiet zone NOT included (the SVG adds its own two modules round it). A project's code is a 29 module symbol, so 28 mm is a 0.97 mm module - over three times the 0.28 mm floor, big enough to read off a laptop screen held at arm's length, and small enough to sit beside the words without taking the panel over. The PDF is rasterised at 144 dpi by default, which is 5.5 pixels a module. It was 34 mm until Adam, 29-Sep-2026, found the hub 'too jump-outy' against the rest of the document and its type came down to the document's own sizes; the code came down with it so the panel stays in proportion.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__QrDarkColourNote: The dark modules of the code: the house navy the whole section is drawn in (the drawings' ink, #172b3a), so the code belongs to the panel it sits in. It is darker than the Project Portal block's grey (#595959) and reads at least as well; an empty or invalid value falls back to that grey. Adam, 29-Sep-2026: the section uses the blue scheme, not the olive.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__TitleTextNote: Also the section's line in the Contents.
TrueVisionHub__LeadInPoints: Every drawing and every document in one place
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__LeadInPointsNote: Quick-reference points under the access panel, in two columns with square markers. Adam, 29-Sep-2026: the one bold lead-in line "reads as one strangely structured sentence" - "make them quick-reference bullet points". Keep each to a few words; four fill the two columns evenly.
TrueVisionHub__LeadParagraphs: Every part of this proposal has been built as a complete three dimensional model and published through TrueVision 3D, Noble Architecture's own project platform. TrueVision is the single home of the whole project. The live model sits alongside a digital copy of every drawing in the pack, the drawing specification, the document register and this statement itself. There is nothing to download and nothing to install. It opens in seconds in any modern web browser on a phone, a tablet or a desktop computer.

TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Heading: Walk Round It Freely
TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Text: Orbit, pan and zoom round the whole scheme, or step down to eye level and walk through it in any direction you choose.

TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Heading: Or Simply Click Through
TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Text: Not confident with 3D controls? A carousel of prepared scenes steps through the key views of the proposal one click at a time.

TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Heading: Every Drawing In Full Detail
TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Text: A digital copy of every sheet in the pack, sharp at any zoom and far closer than paper will ever allow.

TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Heading: Everything In One Place
TrueVisionHub__Tiles.Text: Drawings, specification, document register and statements kept together, so nothing has to be hunted for.

StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__WordsNote: Every sentence here goes into EVERY statement, so none may assume a site: no street, garden, boundary or neighbour. Adam, 29-Sep-2026: "some jobs won't have boundaries and some jobs won't be seen from the street ... genericise it" - hence "from ground level and from a bird's-eye view".
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__TilesNote: Two rows of two. Keep each Text under about 140 characters or the four stop lining up.
TrueVisionHub__CloseParagraphs: This is not a fixed fly through and it is not a reel of flattering viewpoints. The value of this to anyone assessing the scheme is simple. Every claim this statement makes about scale massing and appearance can be confirmed with one's own eyes in a few unhurried minutes rather than taken from the page. Reading a building from flat elevations takes years of training. Walking round it in TrueVision takes seconds. There is no easier way to understand this proposal and no good reason to judge it from paper alone.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__AccessHeadingText: Scan To Step Inside The Model
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__AccessBodyText: Point any phone camera at the code, or select the button. It opens {ProjectName} directly and can be returned to at any time.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__FactsText: Any web browser  ·  Nothing to download  ·  Phone, tablet or desktop
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__FallbackText: Standard Section: TrueVision 3D Project Hub. It is drawn with the project's live link and QR code by TrueVision's Statement Writer; this line is all an editor without it can show.
StatementStandard__TrueVisionHub__Config.TrueVisionHub__FallbackTextNote: What the marker line holds between its tags, so Typora (or anything else that opens the markdown) shows a sentence saying what belongs there rather than nothing.

StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__Description: The drawings that go with the statement: a heading, a line or two of words and a table, all held INSIDE the marker as markdown (a '#' line is the heading, a run of '|' lines is the table, any other line is a paragraph). Adam, 29-Sep-2026: a drawings table that is 'a standardised item that you can toggle on and off', with 'a sync button that can sync it with the live drawing register and pull through all the data, but then still keep it in Markdown or HTML or whatever, so it is editable. It doesn't keep a live link because you might not always want the live link in a document that's meant to be set to a certain date and time'. Sync (on the section's card, and straight after it is switched on) replaces the table's rows with the Drawing Register's - every sheet in tab order, then the Project Specification - and touches nothing else. Between syncs the table is the statement's own.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__LabelNote: What the Standard Sections menu calls it.
DrawingSchedule__NewText: The drawings listed below accompany this statement.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__NewTitleNote: The heading and the words a new schedule starts with. They are the statement's own from then on: retitle it 'Pre-Application Drawing Pack' or anything else in the card's Edit box, and a sync never changes them. The heading is also the section's line in the Contents.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__ColumnsNote: The table's columns, left to right. Key is what each column shows from the register: code (the document code, RB05_T01_D01), name (the sheet's name), label (its tab label, 'D01 - Project Introduction'), scale, size (ISO A2), scaleAndSize ('1:100, ISO A2' in one column), revision (A), status, phase (T01) or drawingNo (D01). Heading is the column's heading; a sync keeps a heading row the writer retitled as long as it still has one heading per column here. Align is left, centre or right.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__SpecificationNote: The Project Specification is listed under the drawings when it holds at least one note: its document number (RB05_SPEC, or whatever number was typed in its bar), this title, this size, and its issued revision. The coded notes on the drawings are consolidated there, so a reader needs to know it is part of the pack. Set IncludeSpecification to false to list drawings only.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__CollapseScaleSuffixNote: A sheet's scale is written the way its title block prints it ('1:100 @ ISO A2'). True prints '1:100' when the row's Size already says ISO A2 - the rule the Drawing Register's PDF uses, so the two documents agree. The sheet's field is never changed.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__EmptyCellTextNote: What a sync writes into a cell the register has nothing for (the specification's scale). The register's own empty-cell mark.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__EmptyText: The table is empty. Press Sync on this section to fill it from the Drawing Register.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__EmptyTextNote: Shown under a table with no rows - in the editor only; the reader, the PDF and the published page never show it.
StatementStandard__DrawingSchedule__Conf.DrawingSchedule__PlaceAfterNote: Where it lands when it is switched on, tried in order: straight above the Document Footer, else after the divider that closes the last numbered section (the Conclusion), else at the end. Always between two major dividers, as its own section, and it can be dragged to another section boundary afterwards.

StatementStandard__DocumentFooter__Confi.DocumentFooter__Description: The end of every statement: the end-of-statement note and the copyright line, drawn as one quiet row under the last major divider - the note to the left, the copyright to the right, 8pt, in the grey the house footer has always shown. The two lines live INSIDE the marker as fields ('End Note: ...', 'Copyright: ...'), so each statement says its own. It is always the last thing in the file, and anything switched on later lands above it. It replaces the two hand-written <h6> lines of the house template, which on RB05 had come apart around the drawing pack, sat with no divider over the copyright, and asked for a colour through 'font-color' - not a CSS property, so it was never drawn. Adam, 29-Sep-2026: 'The footer doesn't seem correct at all.'
DocumentFooter__NewFields: End Note: Note To Reader : End Of Statement
StatementStandard__DocumentFooter__Confi.DocumentFooter__NewFieldsNote: What a statement with no footer of its own is given when the section is switched on; {Year} becomes the year it is switched on, and stays that year. Switched on over the house footer, it takes over the copyright line at the end of the file and an end-of-statement note directly above it instead, words and all. Edit the card's lines to change either; take a line out to leave it off.

StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__Description: The existing-versus-proposed materials table (the design and access statement's 'Material Specification Comparison'), drawn element by element instead of in three narrow columns. Adam, 29-Sep-2026, over RB05's table: 'a table like this doesn't really cut it ... it's not fit for it. We need a better way.' The words stay the writer's own markdown table, held INSIDE the marker one row a line, and are drawn fresh every time: each element's name down the left, its existing finish (small, grey) over its proposed one, each labelled and almost the width of the page; NEW and MATCHES EXISTING tags under the name; every [TO CONFIRM: ...] lifted out of its sentence and set under it as a note; a row with only its first cell filled is a group heading (Walls, Roofs ...); a column headed Status tags each element in the writer's words; any other extra column is one more labelled line. It sits INSIDE a section, under the writer's own '#### N.N |' heading, so the Contents and the numbering are untouched. Switched on, it takes over the first table whose headings read as a comparison (an element column, an existing column, a proposed column), in place; switched off, it writes that table back in the house form.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__LabelNote: What the Standard Sections menu calls it.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__LabelsNote: The small capitals in front of each line, and in front of each lifted [TO CONFIRM] note. The strip over the list prints the table's own headings ('Existing Dwelling', 'Proposed Replacement'); these short labels stay the same on every job so a reader never has to decode them.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__TagsNote: With AutoTags on, an element whose existing cell is one of NoneWords (or empty) is tagged NEW and its empty existing line is left out; one whose proposal matches MatchPattern within a clause ('to strictly match existing', 'identically match the existing profile'), and is not negated ('does not match'), or repeats the existing words exactly, is tagged MATCHES EXISTING. A table column headed Status (or Change) overrides both, row by row, with the writer's own word: New, Matches Existing, Retained, Replaced or anything else.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__NewRowsNote: What a comparison starts with when the statement has no table for it to take over. The headings are the design and access statement skill's; the rows follow its top-down order. Replace each [TO CONFIRM] in the card's Edit box.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__HouseWidthsMmNote: Switched off, the comparison is written back as the house table: the first two headings in inline-block spans of these widths (the skill's 30 mm and 60 mm), every other heading padded to sixty characters, separators of a colon and fifty-nine dashes. RB05's table comes back byte for byte.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__EmptyText: The comparison has no rows yet. Press Edit and add one table row per building element: | **Element** | existing | proposed |.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__EmptyTextNote: Shown under a comparison with no rows - in the editor only; the reader, the PDF and the published page never show it.
StatementStandard__FinishesComparison__C.FinishesComparison__PlaceAfterNote: Where it lands when it is switched on and there is no comparison table to take over: under the block the caret is in (put the caret on the '#### N.N |' heading you want it under, then switch it on). With no caret in the statement it falls back to the registry's default, just above the first numbered section. It does not move with a Move handle: it is part of a section, not a section.
